name: Codeine
route_note: Mainly oral tablets and liquids, often combined with paracetamol or in cough preparations; injection in some countries.

discovery.note: Isolated from opium; most codeine used today is made by methylating morphine.

rx_status: controlled (US Schedule II alone, III–V in combinations; OTC in low-dose combinations in some countries)
tagline: Mild opioid prodrug whose effect depends on CYP2D6 genetics
summary: Codeine is a naturally occurring opium alkaloid used for mild-to-moderate pain, cough and diarrhoea. It is a prodrug converted to morphine by CYP2D6, so its effect and toxicity vary widely between people, leading to restrictions in children.
mechanism: Codeine itself has low affinity for opioid receptors. About 5–10% of a dose is O-demethylated by CYP2D6 to morphine, which produces most of its analgesia by activating mu-opioid receptors.

Poor CYP2D6 metabolisers get little analgesia, while ultrarapid metabolisers convert more codeine to morphine and are at risk of respiratory depression; this has caused deaths in children and breastfed infants. Its antitussive effect acts on the brainstem cough centre.

history.title: Isolation
history.detail: Pierre-Jean Robiquet isolates codeine from opium.

history.title: International control
history.detail: Codeine is listed under the UN Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, with low-dose preparations exempt.

history.title: Breastfeeding death
history.detail: A newborn's death from morphine in breast milk of a mother who was a CYP2D6 ultrarapid metaboliser prompts FDA warnings.

history.title: Paediatric restrictions
history.detail: The FDA adds a boxed warning about deaths after tonsillectomy in children; the EMA restricts use under 12 years.

history.title: US contraindication
history.detail: The FDA contraindicates codeine for pain or cough in children under 12.

history.title: Australia upscheduling
history.detail: Australia makes all codeine-containing medicines prescription-only.

pk.metabolism: hepatic: CYP2D6 to morphine, CYP3A4 to norcodeine, UGT2B7 to codeine-6-glucuronide

serious: Respiratory depression (especially in CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolisers)
Fatal toxicity in children and breastfed infants
safety.boxed_warning: Addiction, abuse and misuse; life-threatening respiratory depression; ultrarapid metabolism of codeine and death in children; interactions with CYP3A4 inhibitors and with benzodiazepines.

facts: About 1–10% of people (depending on ancestry) are CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolisers; the proportion is particularly high in some North African and Middle Eastern populations.

references.title: FDA Drug Safety Communication on codeine and tramadol in children (2017)
